purpose: Prior-art seed for the next longevity mission rerun. This record is a source pointer and claim map, not a validated ORACLE finding.
novelty_policy: The 8-mRPG signature and its association with transcriptomic aging are published prior art. ORACLE must not claim this signature itself as a novel discovery.

sources.title: Preserved mitochondrial ribosomal protein gene expression marks a youthful transcriptional state in Chinese nonagenarians and centenarians
claims: The abstract reports 1,751 analyzed individuals (811 LLIs and 940 younger controls); the Methods section reports 1,752 recruited individuals (811 LLIs and 941 younger controls), with one previously published sample excluded for missing age.
Eight mitochondrial ribosomal protein genes showed upward deviation from the typical age-related decline trajectory in long-lived individuals.
The 8-mRPG expression score was associated with lower transcriptomic aging and senescence-related scores.
The authors report replication of the signature pattern in additional longevity cohorts, including the Leiden Longevity Study.
limitations: The study is observational and cross-sectional; it does not establish that mRPG expression causes longevity.
The upstream regulatory processes maintaining mRPG expression remain unknown.
The authors call for functional experiments and note residual confounding may remain.

The paper contains a sample-count discrepancy: 1,751 vs 1,752 total participants and 441 vs 442 previously reported samples (171 CRA000515 + 271 HRA000656); one missing-age exclusion is mentioned. Resolve against the source manifest before analysis.

data_accessions.note: The paper's key-resource table lists 171 CRA000515 + 271 HRA000656 = 442 previously reported samples; Methods state one sample lacked age and was excluded, while the Data Availability Statement reports 441 deposited samples. This count discrepancy must be reconciled from sample-level metadata before analysis.

next_checks: Obtain sample-level metadata and mapping for CRA000515 aliases.
Verify the integrated expression matrix sample annotations and cohort overlap before treating datasets as independent.
Reproduce the 8-mRPG signature with the published code and exact cohort splits.
Test robustness to leukocyte composition, sex, region, sequencing batch, and age.
Generate and experimentally test upstream-regulator hypotheses; do not infer causality from expression associations.

independent_evidence.design: mouse genetics plus C. elegans RNAi and mammalian-cell experiments
independent_evidence.finding: MRPS5 and other mitochondrial ribosomal protein perturbations induced mitonuclear protein imbalance and UPRmt; MRPS5 knockdown extended C. elegans lifespan.
independent_evidence.relevance: Functional model-organism evidence that mitochondrial translation perturbation can influence lifespan.
independent_evidence.limitation: Direction differs from the higher-than-age-expected expression of selected mRPGs reported in long-lived humans; model-organism intervention is not proof of human causality.

independent_evidence.design: human skeletal-muscle ribosome profiling across middle-aged and older adults
independent_evidence.finding: Older age was associated with lower ribosome occupancy for multiple mitochondrial-genome-encoded oxidative-phosphorylation transcripts.
independent_evidence.relevance: Independent human tissue evidence that mitochondrial translation is age-sensitive.
independent_evidence.limitation: Does not measure the 8-mRPG signature or exceptional longevity; mitochondrial-genome-encoded OXPHOS translation is distinct from nuclear-encoded mitochondrial ribosomal-protein transcript abundance.

independent_evidence.design: human Mendelian-randomization analysis of translation-machinery expression
independent_evidence.finding: Genetically proxied expression of Pol I/III machinery and ribosomal-protein genes was associated with human longevity; reduced expression in several tissues was reported as longevity-associated.
independent_evidence.relevance: Supports a possible global/cytosolic translation-reduction arm of healthy aging.
independent_evidence.limitation: Not specific to mitochondrial ribosomal proteins; MR depends on instrument validity and does not validate the 8-mRPG mechanism.

independent_evidence.design: two Chinese longevity cohorts plus cell perturbation assays
independent_evidence.finding: 185 long-lived individuals and 86 offspring spouses showed downregulated cytosolic ribosome pathway; ETS1 was lower in long-lived individuals and ETS1 knockdown reduced cytosolic ribosomal-protein gene expression and cellular senescence in fibroblast models.
independent_evidence.relevance: Provides a plausible contrast between reduced cytosolic ribosome biogenesis and preserved selected mitochondrial ribosomal transcripts.
independent_evidence.limitation: Cytosolic ribosomal genes are not mitochondrial ribosomal genes; cell assays do not establish a whole-organism longevity mechanism.

hypothesis_audit.title: Compartment-specific translation allocation in long-lived humans
hypothesis_audit.statement: Long-lived individuals may preserve a selected mitochondrial ribosomal transcript program above age-expected levels while allowing broader cytosolic ribosome biogenesis to decline; this could help maintain mitochondrial protein synthesis without maintaining globally high translation.
hypothesis_audit.key_alternative: Blood-cell composition, regional/batch effects, or survivor/health selection may explain part of the bulk-expression signature.
falsifiable_tests: Recompute the exact 8-mRPG score from frozen sample-level counts in independent cohorts with matched tissue and verified phenotype.
Test the score within sorted or single-cell-defined leukocyte populations and after cell-composition, sex, age, region and batch adjustment.
Test whether the score predicts mitochondrial translation, mitochondrial-encoded OXPHOS protein abundance, respiratory capacity or ATP production.
Use graded perturbation and rescue of the exact published 8 genes in relevant human cell models; measure mitochondrial translation, respiration, UPRmt and senescence.

hypothesis_audit.title: Dose- and tissue-dependent mitonuclear stress hormesis
hypothesis_audit.statement: Partial or transient mitochondrial translation disruption may activate mitonuclear protein imbalance and UPRmt, whereas preservation of a subset of mitochondrial ribosomal genes may be beneficial in selected human tissues or late-life states; effects may be dose-, tissue- and time-dependent.
falsifiable_tests: Run graded rather than binary perturbations of candidate mRPGs and mitochondrial translation regulators.
Measure time-resolved mitonuclear protein stoichiometry, UPRmt, respiration and cell survival.
Determine whether transient versus chronic perturbation produces opposite effects.

hypothesis_audit.title: Bulk-blood cell-composition or health-status confounding
hypothesis_audit.statement: The 8-mRPG bulk-blood association may partly reflect differences in leukocyte subtype proportions, immune activation, medication, nutritional status or cohort selection rather than a cell-intrinsic longevity mechanism.
falsifiable_tests: Repeat analysis with measured cell counts and cell-type deconvolution in every cohort.
Test within-cell-type expression using sorted cells or single-cell RNA-seq.
Adjust for medication, BMI, diet, chronic disease and sequencing/library protocol where available.

gates: The 2026 8-mRPG signature is prior art; ORACLE must not claim it as a new discovery.
The 2013 MRPS5/UPRmt intervention literature and 2026 human expression signature have different directions and biological contexts; reconcile rather than cherry-pick.
The 2021 human muscle translation study concerns mitochondrial-genome-encoded OXPHOS translation, not the same nuclear-encoded mRPG transcript signature.
The 2022 ETS1 and Mendelian-randomization findings concern broad/cytosolic translation machinery, not direct replication of the 8-mRPG signature.
No mechanism passes novelty or causality review until independent sample-level replication and functional perturbation/rescue are complete.
